title: David Almona
text:
David Almona
Welcome! I’m an analytics professional with experience in statistical modeling, and sports analytics, focused on analyzing complex datasets, communicating insights to stakeholders, and building solutions that contribute to organizational impact.
I also enjoy working on sports analytics projects and have used R, Python, SQL, and BI tools on my projects. Also, I have a number of research, internships, and conference presentation experiences.

title: Projects
text:
Featured Projects



Jun 2026 | Personal Project


2026 FIFA World Cup Prediction
Using a Poisson regression model and Monte Carlo simulations to project tournament outcomes.
Result: Finished 4th of 47 entries in a public prediction contest on X, ranking 2nd by Brier score.

Write-up | GitHub





Mar 2026 | Take-Home Task


Houston Dynamo Forward Recruitment Analysis
Analyzed 2024 MLS season data from SkillCorner and Wyscout to identify and recommend a forward signing based on physical, athletic, and production metrics.

Slides | GitHub

Chasing Imperfect Passes: Into the Life of a Receiver
Evaluating how a quarterback’s throw makes life easier or harder for the receiver by quantifying receiver adjustments while the ball is in the air.
Partner: Sammy Davis

Forced Turnover: Evaluating Pressing Effectiveness in Soccer
A machine learning approach to analyze pressing in soccer with player-tracking data from MLS matches in the 2023 season.
Partners: Natalie Rayce (Carnegie Mellon University) and Daniel Wicker (Charlotte FC)

title: David Almona
text:
Born and raised in Lagos, Nigeria, I completed my B.S. in Economics with a minor in Data Science from Centre College in May 2026. I also competed in the 100m and 200m as a collegiate track and field athlete.
I enjoy working on data science and analytical problems in sports and continue to develop my skills in Python, statistical modeling, and machine learning while keeping up with developments in the field.
In my free time, I enjoy watching and playing sports, going to the gym, and listening to contemporary gospel worship and AfroGospel, among others.
